shipped_rows.title_o: Run for the team: An analysis of effort gains in track and field relays

blind_target.evidence_quote: In a replication and extension of this study, we wanted to find out whether its findings replicate in a sample of 1,718 observations from 1,270 U.S. college athletes and whether effort expenditure is driven by working in a team or the chance of valuable outcomes in the relay.
blind_target.outcome_quote: As shown by linear mixed modeling and regression analyses, runners exhibited effort gains only if their relays had high medal chances and if they had not been successful in the individual competition (i.e., did not place first to third). Moreover, relay members who had been successful in the individual competition showed effort losses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original effort gains are stated and the replication finds them only under restricted conditions, with losses in others; provisionally mixed. Complete reference entry is not present in the saved abstract; no citation metadata guessed.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract explicitly says the present study replicates Schleu et al. (2019) and describes the same team effort gain finding in 400-m runners. Supplied shipped row 495 is that same original by DOI, title, authors, and year.

luna_triage.identity_quote: In 2019, Schleu et al. showed that 400-m runners at major championships exhibited team effort gains-they ran faster in the relay than in the individual competition.
